title: File a task from CI
description: Put failed builds on the task board for an agent to pick up.

sections.title: GitHub Actions step
paragraphs: Store the office’s public URL and a dedicated token as repository secrets. The run id doubles as the idempotency key, so re-running the step never files a second task.
sections.code:
# .github/workflows/nightly.yml (excerpt)
- name: File a task when the nightly build fails
  if: failure()
  env:
    BUREAU_URL: ${{ secrets.BUREAU_URL }}
    BUREAU_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUREAU_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$BUREAU_URL/api/tasks" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $BUREAU_TOKEN" \
      -H "Idempotency-Key: nightly-${{ github.run_id }}" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "$(jq -n --arg url "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
        '{title: "Nightly build failed", description: $url, priority: "P1"}')"

sections.title: Notes
paragraphs: The runner calls the office from outside, so the office needs a public HTTPS URL. To react to GitHub events directly instead of from a workflow, use an inbound webhook.
